name: Muhsen
mission: MUHSEN aims for both better communities and better daily lives for all adults and children who are living with disabilities.
theoryOfChange: Muhsen, a US-based non-profit organization, has a documented strategic framework that outlines its approach to creating an inclusive and accessible environment for individuals with disabilities within the Muslim community. Their mission is to advocate, educate, train, and implement programs and services across North America to improve the experience within mosques, conventions, classes, and events, fostering a positive community for those with disabilities. The organization's strategic plan was supported during its launch to help families with disabilities gain access to community events and mosques. Muhsen's approach includes a Masjid Certification program, which evaluates and certifies mosques based on criteria for accommodating individuals with special needs. They also offer Service Certification to help other organizations become accessible. Furthermore, Muhsen conducts a Needs Research Report to collect data and inform their work, ensuring they meet the present and future needs of the community. This comprehensive approach, encompassing their mission, vision, strategic initiatives, and certification programs, serves as their impact framework, detailing how their activities lead to their desired societal changes.

strengths_deep_dive: Muhsen serves a critically underserved niche by supporting individuals with intellectual, physical, and mental disabilities within Muslim spaces. Its programmatic work focuses on actionable community integration, ranging from respite services to mosque accessibility standards. Grounding its efforts in empirical data, Muhsen has evaluated <cite id="4">1,982 survey respondents</cite> to map special needs within local populations. A key operational highlight was organizing a specialized pilgrimage that supported <cite id="11">58 pilgrims on an accessible Umrah trip</cite>. Furthermore, the charity holds a <cite id="14">Candid Platinum Seal of Transparency</cite> and maintains a low fundraising cost of <cite id="14">$0.07 per $1 raised</cite>.
rich_narrative.summary: Muhsen is a North American nonprofit dedicated to serving individuals with special needs and establishing inclusive environments within Muslim communities <cite id="3">across the United States and Canada</cite>. The organization's core operations include mosque accessibility certification, weekend educational programming, respite care, and specialized travel initiatives. In FY2024, Muhsen reported <cite id="1">a total revenue of $3,305,007</cite>. A notable programmatic achievement includes organizing an <cite id="11">inaugural accessible Umrah pilgrimage for 58 individuals</cite> with special needs. Despite strong program design and clear outcome tracking, the organization's financial deployment profile presents notable tradeoffs. In FY2024, Muhsen operated with a <cite id="14">program expense ratio of 57.4%</cite>, which falls below the standard 75% sector benchmark for spending efficiency. Additionally, financial filings show <cite id="14">working capital reserves covering 37.9 months of working capital</cite>. For a zakat-collecting charity, holding nearly three years of operating reserves creates a potential delay between donor contributions and direct community impact, balancing financial stability against immediate field deployment.
